page.overview:
Who is Lanfear?

Lanfear was known to have been as strong as a woman could be in the One Power. Her strength level of is only equalled by Alivia and Semirhage. This level was reduced to by the Finn after they fed on her ability to channel. When reincarnated as Cyndane, this loss of strength was not restored.

While the books occasionally refer to her as being the second most powerful of the Forsaken after Ishamael, she is weaker than all of the male Forsaken in terms of raw power. It should be noted that the strongest male is roughly equivalent to the strongest female, in terms of what they can do with the One Power. Women can weave much more deftly than men, which compensates for strength differences. We should therefore consider Lanfear as being one of the Forsaken's most dangerous channelers.

Lanfear is a Dreamwalker skilled in various aspects of the Dreamworld. She considered Tel'aran'rhiod to be her "personal property". In conversation with "Ba'alzamon", she chides him for making "free use of her domain". Although she liked to claim that no one was more skilled there than she, a fact that was still remembered in the Third Age, this was not true. Birgitte says that Moghedien "could do things here far beyond Lanfear, though she has not Lanfear's strength in the world of flesh." While Ishamael himself was also a Dreamwalker, their comparative skill levels are unknown.

Perrin Aybara's defeat of Lanfear in the World of Dreams would initially point to her not being as skilled as previously thought. Ten years after the publication of A Memory of Light, Brandon Sanderson revealed that she had merely faked her own death by skillfully manipulating the dreamworld., Brandon Sanderson on The Dusty Wheel.}}

Also known as: Mierin, Mierin Eronaile, Cyndane.
